lessons.title: Production of Garri: Traditional and Improved Methods
lessons.body: Garri is the most common cassava product in West Africa. To make garri, you need fresh cassava roots, a grater, a press, a sieve, and a frying pan or a garri fryer. Start by peeling and washing the roots. Grate them into a fine mash. Traditional grating uses a handmade metal sheet with punched holes, but an engine-powered grater saves time and produces finer mash. After grating, put the mash into a porous sack and press it for 2-3 days to remove water. This fermentation gives garri its sour taste. For improved method, use a hydraulic press to reduce moisture to about 40-45% in just 30 minutes. Then sieve the pressed mash to break lumps. You can use a woven basket sieve or a mechanical sifter. Now fry the sieved mash in a hot pan or a continuous garri fryer. Stir constantly with a wooden paddle. Fry until the garri turns light yellow or white and crisp, about 15-20 minutes for a large pan. For improved method, use a stainless steel fryer with a rotating paddle and a firewood or gas burner. This can fry 50 kg per hour. After frying, spread the garri to cool, then sieve again to remove any burnt particles. Package in clean bags or plastic containers. Good garri is dry, crispy, and has a sour taste. It can last 6 months if kept dry. You can sell plain garri or add palm oil to make yellow garri. A 50 kg bag of fresh roots yields about 10-12 kg of garri. With improved methods, you reduce labour and increase output.
lessons.title: Fufu and Lafun Processing
Fufu and Lafun Processing
lessons.body: Fufu and lafun are fermented cassava products eaten as swallow foods. Fufu is made from fresh cassava, while lafun uses dried cassava chips. For fufu, peel and wash cassava roots. Soak them in water for 3-4 days to ferment. The water should cover the roots completely. After soaking, the roots become soft. Remove the fibres and pound the soft roots in a wooden mortar with a pestle until smooth. You can also use a mechanical blender or a hammer mill for large scale. The pounded fufu is then sieved to remove lumps. Traditional fufu is sold wet and must be cooked before eating. To cook, put the fufu paste in a pot, add water, and stir over fire until it thickens into a smooth dough. For improved method, you can dry the fufu paste into flour. Spread the wet fufu on a tray and sun-dry for 2-3 days, then mill into powder. This fufu flour can be stored for months. For lafun, peel and wash cassava, then soak in water for 3-4 days. Remove, slice into thin chips, and sun-dry for 2-3 days until brittle. Mill the dried chips into flour. Lafun flour is white and fine. To prepare lafun, mix the flour with boiling water and stir until it forms a smooth dough. Both fufu and lafun are eaten with soups like efo riro or egusi. For business, package fufu flour in 1 kg or 5 kg bags. A 100 kg of fresh roots yields about 30 kg of fufu flour or 25 kg of lafun flour. Use a mechanical press to remove excess water from fufu before drying to speed up the process.
lessons.title: Cassava Flour and Starch Production
Cassava Flour and Starch Production
lessons.body: Cassava flour is a fine powder made from dried cassava roots. It is used for baking, thickening soups, and making snacks. High-quality cassava flour (HQCF) is popular in Nigeria and Ghana. To make cassava flour, peel and wash fresh roots. Grate the roots into a mash. Press the mash to remove water using a hydraulic press or a screw press. The pressed cake should have about 40-50% moisture. Break the cake into small pieces and dry them in the sun on a raised platform or in a solar dryer for 2-3 days until the moisture is below 10%. Dry chips should be brittle and break easily. Mill the dried chips in a hammer mill or a disc mill to get fine flour. Sieve the flour through a 250-micron sieve to remove coarse particles. Package the flour in airtight bags. Cassava starch is different from flour. Starch is the pure carbohydrate extracted from cassava. To make starch, grate fresh roots and mix the mash with water. Sieve the mixture to remove fibres. Let the milky liquid settle in a tank for 4-6 hours. The starch settles at the bottom. Pour off the water and scrape the starch. Wash the starch again with clean water, then dry it in the sun or in an oven at 50-60Â°C. The dried starch is a fine white powder. Cassava starch is used in industries for making glue, textiles, and food. For business, you can sell cassava flour to bakeries or starch to factories. A tonne of fresh roots yields about 200-250 kg of cassava flour or 150-200 kg of starch. Use a mechanical peeler and grater to increase efficiency.
lessons.title: Tapioca and Other Snack Products
Tapioca and Other Snack Products
lessons.body: Tapioca is a snack made from cassava starch. It is popular in Nigeria, Ghana, and Brazil. To make tapioca, you need cassava starch, water, and a frying pan. Mix starch with a little water to form a paste. Heat a non-stick pan and spread a thin layer of the paste. Cook for 1-2 minutes until it forms a flexible sheet. Add fillings like grated coconut, groundnuts, or fish, then fold and serve. For a crispy snack, deep-fry the tapioca sheets. Another snack is cassava chips. Peel and wash cassava roots. Slice into thin rounds using a mandoline or a sharp knife. Soak the slices in salted water for 10 minutes, then drain. Deep-fry in hot oil at 170Â°C until golden brown. Remove and drain on paper. Season with salt, pepper, or spices. Package in airtight bags. Cassava chin-chin is another snack. Mix cassava flour with wheat flour, sugar, butter, and eggs. Knead into a dough, cut into small cubes, and deep-fry until golden. Cassava doughnuts: mix cassava flour with yeast, sugar, and water, let it rise, then fry in oil. Cassava puff-puff: similar to doughnuts but with cassava flour. For business, these snacks sell well in schools, markets, and bus parks. You can start with a small fryer and a few kg of cassava flour. A 50 kg bag of cassava flour can make about 200 packs of snacks. Ensure hygiene: wear gloves, use clean oil, and package attractively. Snacks have a short shelf life of 1-2 weeks, so sell fresh. You can also add value by using vacuum sealing to extend shelf life.
lessons.title: Cassava-Based Animal Feed Formulation
Cassava-Based Animal Feed Formulation
lessons.body: Cassava can be used to make animal feed for poultry, pigs, and cattle. Dried cassava chips or peels are ground into cassava meal. This meal is high in energy but low in protein, so it must be mixed with other ingredients. For poultry feed, use 40-50% cassava meal, 30% maize, 15% soybean meal, 3% fish meal, 1% limestone, and 1% vitamin premix. Mix all ingredients thoroughly in a feed mixer or on a clean concrete floor. This feed can replace maize in poultry diets and reduce cost by 20-30%. For pigs, use 50% cassava meal, 20% maize, 20% soybean meal, 5% fish meal, 3% palm kernel cake, and 2% mineral premix. Pigs grow well on this feed. For cattle, you can use cassava peels and leaves. Cassava leaves must be wilted or dried to remove cyanide. Sun-dry the leaves for 2-3 days, then grind them into leaf meal. Mix 30% cassava leaf meal with 70% cassava peel meal and add molasses for energy. This feed is good for dairy cows and goats. To make feed, you need a hammer mill, a mixer, and a weighing scale. Always test for cyanide: grate a small sample, add water, and let it sit for 30 minutes. If it smells bitter, it has high cyanide. Proper drying and fermentation reduce cyanide. For business, you can produce and sell feed in 50 kg bags. A small feed mill can produce 1 tonne per day. Source cassava peels from garri processing centres for free or cheap. This turns waste into profit. Ensure feed is dry and stored in a cool, dry place to prevent mould.
lessons.title: Value Addition: Chips, Pellets, and Ethanol
Value Addition: Chips, Pellets, and Ethanol
lessons.body: Cassava chips are dried pieces of cassava used for export and industrial use. To make chips, peel and wash fresh roots. Slice into chips of 2-3 cm thickness using a chipping machine or a sharp knife. Spread the chips on a drying rack and sun-dry for 3-4 days until moisture is below 14%. Turn them daily for even drying. Dried chips are packed in jute bags or woven polypropylene bags for export to China, Europe, and other countries. A tonne of fresh roots yields about 300-350 kg of dried chips. Price for export is around $200-300 per tonne. Pellets are made by compressing cassava chips or mash into small cylindrical pieces. Use a pellet machine. Pellets are easier to store and transport. They are used for animal feed and for ethanol production. Ethanol is a biofuel made from cassava starch. The process involves gelatinization, saccharification, fermentation, and distillation. First, mill cassava chips into flour. Mix with water to form a slurry. Heat to 80-90Â°C to gelatinize the starch. Cool to 60Â°C and add enzymes (alpha-amylase) to break down starch into sugars. Then add yeast and ferment for 48-72 hours. The fermented mash contains about 10-15% ethanol. Distill the mash in a distillation unit to get 95% pure ethanol. This ethanol can be used as fuel or in industries. A small ethanol plant can process 1 tonne of cassava chips to produce 300-350 litres of ethanol. For business, you can start with chips and pellets, which require less capital. Ethanol requires more investment but has high returns. Always ensure quality control: test moisture, ash, and starch content. Work with export agents to find buyers. Value addition increases income and reduces post-harvest losses.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of pressing grated cassava mash during garri production?
quiz.explanation: Pressing removes water and helps fermentation, which gives garri its sour taste.

quiz.q: Which tool is used to fry garri in an improved method?
quiz.explanation: A stainless steel fryer with a rotating paddle is used for large-scale garri frying.

quiz.q: How long should cassava roots be soaked to make fufu?
quiz.explanation: Soaking for 3-4 days ferments the roots and softens them for pounding.

quiz.q: What is lafun made from?
quiz.explanation: Lafun is made from fermented and dried cassava chips that are milled into flour.

quiz.q: What is the moisture content of pressed cassava cake for flour production?
quiz.explanation: The pressed cake should have about 40-50% moisture before drying.

quiz.q: Which sieve size is used to get fine cassava flour?
quiz.explanation: A 250-micron sieve removes coarse particles and gives fine flour.

quiz.q: How is cassava starch extracted from grated cassava?
quiz.explanation: Starch settles at the bottom when the milky liquid is left to stand.

quiz.q: What is tapioca made from?
quiz.explanation: Tapioca is a snack made from cassava starch mixed with water and cooked.

quiz.q: At what temperature should cassava chips be deep-fried?
quiz.explanation: Frying at 170Â°C gives crispy chips without burning.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is used to add protein to cassava-based poultry feed?
quiz.explanation: Soybean meal is a protein source that balances the low protein in cassava.

quiz.q: Why must cassava leaves be dried before using in animal feed?
quiz.explanation: Drying reduces cyanide content, making the leaves safe for animals.

quiz.q: What is the moisture content of dried cassava chips for export?
quiz.explanation: Dried chips should have moisture below 14% to prevent mould and meet export standards.

quiz.q: What is the first step in ethanol production from cassava?
quiz.explanation: Gelatinization involves heating the cassava slurry to break down starch.

quiz.q: How many litres of ethanol can be produced from 1 tonne of cassava chips?
quiz.explanation: A small ethanol plant can produce about 300-350 litres from a tonne of chips.

quiz.q: Which of these is a traditional method of grating cassava?
options: B) Handmade metal sheet with punched holes
quiz.explanation: Traditional grating uses a punched metal sheet, while modern methods use powered graters.

quiz.q: What is the yield of garri from 50 kg of fresh cassava roots?
quiz.explanation: About 10-12 kg of garri is obtained from 50 kg of fresh roots.

quiz.q: Which fermentation time is needed for fufu production?
quiz.explanation: Soaking for 3-4 days ferments the cassava for fufu.

quiz.q: What is the main difference between cassava flour and cassava starch?
options: A) Flour is pure carbohydrate, starch is not
B) Starch is pure carbohydrate, flour contains other components
D) Flour is used only for animal feed
quiz.explanation: Starch is extracted pure carbohydrate, while flour contains fibre and other parts of the root.

quiz.q: Which snack is made by deep-frying thin slices of cassava?
quiz.explanation: Cassava chips are thin slices that are deep-fried until crispy.

quiz.q: What percentage of cassava meal is recommended in poultry feed?
quiz.explanation: Cassava meal can replace 40-50% of maize in poultry diets.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of adding molasses to cattle feed?
quiz.explanation: Molasses is a source of energy and improves palatability.

quiz.q: Which machine is used to compress cassava mash into pellets?
quiz.explanation: A pellet machine compresses cassava mash into small cylindrical pellets.

quiz.q: What is the final ethanol concentration after fermentation?
quiz.explanation: Fermented mash typically contains 10-15% ethanol before distillation.

quiz.q: Which of these is a key quality control test for cassava chips?
quiz.explanation: Moisture content is critical for preventing mould and meeting export standards.

quiz.q: What is the yield of cassava flour from 1 tonne of fresh roots?
quiz.explanation: About 200-250 kg of cassava flour is obtained from a tonne of fresh roots.

quiz.q: Which of these is a traditional method of pressing cassava mash?
quiz.explanation: Traditionally, mash is put in a sack and pressed with stones or a wooden press.

quiz.q: What is the shelf life of well-dried garri?
quiz.explanation: Good garri can last up to 6 months if kept dry and away from moisture.

quiz.q: Which enzyme is used to break down starch into sugars for ethanol?
quiz.explanation: Alpha-amylase breaks down starch into simpler sugars during saccharification.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of cassava pellets over chips?
options: B) Easier to store and transport
quiz.explanation: Pellets are denser and easier to handle, store, and transport than loose chips.

quiz.q: Which of these is a value-added cassava product for export?
quiz.explanation: Dried cassava chips are a major export commodity for industrial use.
